observation_summary: The SingularValueDecomposition implementation produced incorrect results (NaNs) for rank-deficient matrices because the algorithm for computing the U matrix (specifically the W matrix calculation) was flawed in its iteration bounds and handling of the bidiagonal elements.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves rewriting the loop structure and the computational logic for calculating the matrix W. The original code had incorrect loop bounds (p-1) and a separate, incorrectly placed block for the final iteration. The fix unifies the loop to cover all elements (up to p) and introduces conditional logic to correctly handle the bidiagonal elements (main and secondary) within the computation, which is a procedural/algorithmic correction.
evidence_used: The fix modifies the loop bounds from 'i < p - 1' to 'i < p'.
The fix removes a separate, incorrectly placed block for the final iteration.
The fix introduces an 'if (i < n - 1)' condition to correctly apply the secondary bidiagonal element only when appropriate, ensuring the computation of 'wi[j]' is correct for all indices.
The fix changes the submatrix extraction range from 'p - 1' to 'n - 1' (or 'm - 1'), indicating an incorrect assumption about the matrix dimensions in the original algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds an 'if' condition, the primary purpose is to correct the computational logic of the SVD algorithm, not to validate input parameters or guard against invalid states.
The fix is not about correcting a single wrong value or initialization, but about restructuring the entire computational loop and the logic used to derive the matrix values.
